title: PLEASE Verdict
description: The machine-readable result of one scan. This document is the caller-facing contract: an agent harness or pre-tool hook reads this and applies its own policy. Additive fields are a minor version change; removing or retyping a field is a breaking change.

outcome.description: The three-way result. `clean` requires both an empty `reasons` array and an empty `incomplete` array. Analysis that did not complete is never reported as `clean`. Precedence: risk_found outranks inconclusive, which outranks clean.

score.description: Aggregate risk on a fixed integer scale: the highest single reason severity, plus 5 for each distinct detection class beyond the highest-scoring one, bonus capped at 15 and total capped at 100. Computed over every match found, before `reasons` is truncated. Insensitive to input length and to match count, so a long benign document cannot accrue risk by size alone. Integer rather than fractional so repeated runs are byte-identical across hosts.

risk.description: Human-facing band derived from `score` by the rule set's band table.

reasons.description: Supporting observations, sorted by (span.start, rule_id) for reproducibility. Length is bounded by the policy's max_reasons independently of input length.

reasons_truncated.description: True when the max_reasons bound dropped observations. A truncated list is never presented as complete.

incomplete.description: Everything the scan did not examine, whether because a configured bound was reached or because something failed. Non-empty means coverage was incomplete. Empty (together with empty `reasons`) is the only case in which `clean` is permitted.

suppressed.description: AMENDED BY 002 (FR-128), ADDED TO THIS SCHEMA AT 001 T065. Observations that suppression hid, each annotated with what hid it. These are NOT findings: they do not score, they do not affect the outcome, and a verdict whose only content is suppressions is `clean`. They are here so a reader can answer "what did the heuristic change?" from one scan rather than from a second run with --no-suppress-in-quotes. Deliberately a separate array from `reasons` rather than a flag on them, because one list with a boolean leaves the distinction to every reader to remember, and the reader who forgets reintroduces every security-prose false positive.

suppressions_truncated.description: True when more was suppressed than the reason bound reports. Unlike `reasons_truncated` this is NOT a coverage gap: the reader is not being shown the whole of something they are not being shown at all.

judge_report.description: Present only on a verdict the judgement tier acted on (feature 004, FR-416). Its ABSENCE is meaningful: it says the verdict is purely structural and 001's SC-011 determinism guarantee applies to it unchanged. Its presence with every span `confirmed` is a different statement from absence — one verdict has a second opinion behind it and the other does not. The raw model response is deliberately NOT recorded: it is attacker-influenced text with no consumer, and storing it would create a channel by which content reaches a reader that the sanitisation path never inspected.

model.description: Resolved model id. A verdict judged by one model is not evidence about another.

prompt_version.description: Changes the answers as surely as the model does, and is the variable we control.

features.description: The document-level answers, as returned. Recorded because the score is computed from them (FR-407) — without them it is an unexplained number.

relation.description: ADDED AT 001 T065; it should have arrived with 004 plan D4a and did not. Whether the excerpt is the document's SUBJECT or a PASSENGER inside it. D4a calls it "the field that decides the case": `span_role` and every document-level field answer IDENTICALLY for the two discriminating fixtures — correctly, and uselessly, because at document scale a transcript displaying payloads and one carrying a payload are the same document. This is the question that separates them, and it agreed with hand labels 12/12 where `span_role` managed 14/20.

judgement.description: TWO values, and that is the security property (FR-403). There is no `cleared`, no `escalated`, and no `added` — not validated against, but not representable, which is why SC-406's property test checks a type rather than a code path.

rule_id.description: Stable namespaced identifier. Also the handle a caller uses to suppress this rule.

class.description: Detection family: the KIND of finding, never how it was delivered. A payload recovered by decoding carries the class of the rule that matched it; the delivery is in `chain`. AMENDED by feature 003 (FR-301): `agent_directed` was added — content that addresses the reading agent rather than the human the document is for, which no other class describes. AMENDED again: `external_action` was added — an instruction to act on state outside the conversation (grant access, approve a record, transfer funds), which `solicitation` does not describe because it asks for nothing belonging to the agent. Added on measurement rather than taxonomy: it fires on 85 of 1,054 adversarial InjecAgent rows that no other rule reaches, for one additional false positive in 4,492 benign documents. AMENDED by feature 005 (FR-506): `privilege` was added — content that widens the agent's OWN authority (auto-approval, a permission allow-list, a bypass mode, a safety flag removed). Distinct from `external_action`, which acts on state outside the agent: one is an action taken through the guardrail, the other is an attack on the guardrail. Added because a caller's policy may reasonably block the second while merely logging the first, and with seven classes that distinction was unrepresentable. AMENDED by feature 002 (FR-131): `encoding` was removed. It named a delivery mechanism, no rule could declare it, and it was applied only by the decode path — so a decoded finding had to satisfy two different class filters and no single selection satisfied both.

matched.description: Excerpt of the matching content, already neutralised so it cannot forge, erase, or reorder surrounding output, and truncated to the policy's max_excerpt_bytes.

chain.description: Decoding steps that led to this match. Empty for a direct match. Non-empty means the payload was recovered by decoding, and the rule fired on the decoded content rather than on the encoding's presence.

description.description: Why this rule exists, carried from the rule definition so a finding explains itself without a lookup.

suppressed_by.description: What suppressed this observation. On a reason in `suppressed`, it names what moved it there. On a reason in `reasons`, it means a quoting context WOULD have suppressed it and policy disabled suppression. Widened by feature 004 (T009): `judge` joins the quoting contexts, because the judgement tier is a second author of the same sentence and a judge-demoted observation is not *quoted* — see specs/004-judgement-tier/data-model.md.

span.description: Half-open byte range into the ORIGINAL input, never into decoded content, so a caller can always highlight bytes the user actually holds.

kind.description: The five transformation families labelled in the evaluation corpus, plus the two Unicode concealment channels that carry decodable payloads.

decoded_excerpt.description: The recovered content that triggered the rule. Neutralised and truncated as `matched` is.

incompleteness.description: One thing the scan did not examine. Causes divide into bounds the caller configured (which carry `configured`, and can be raised) and failures in the environment (which do not, and must be fixed). One list rather than two, so the `clean` invariant remains a check on a single field.

cause.description: Bounds: input_size, decode_depth, max_matches_per_rule, max_reasons, excerpt_length. Failures: target_unreadable (a file in a directory walk could not be read — the walk continues and this target is inconclusive, never silently skipped), target_not_traversed (a symbolic link to a directory, which a walk refuses to follow because it may be a cycle — the path is readable and the caller declined, which is why it is not target_unreadable), decode_failed, ruleset_unavailable, tier_unavailable (an optional detection tier was not available, which degrades to inconclusive and never to clean).

configured.description: The value in force when a bound was reached, so a caller can raise it deliberately. Present for bound causes, absent for failure causes.

detail.description: What went unexamined — which rule saturated, which region was skipped, why a target could not be read.

target_ref.description: What was scanned. Reporting metadata only: nothing here influences judgement.

name.description: Caller-supplied label or the path exactly as given. Never absolutised, so output does not vary by working directory.

ruleset_id.description: Identity of the resolved rule set: built-in default plus caller additions and suppressions. Two verdicts carrying the same values were produced by the same rules.

digest.description: Content digest over the resolved rule set, so an old verdict can be attributed to exact rules.
